Specify a Multi-Facet LLM Coding Design

Source: R/coding.R
coding_design.Rd

Defines a crossed experimental coding design (prompts x models x temperatures x replicates) paired with a strict coding_schema() for reproducible LLM measurement studies.

Usage

coding_design(
  prompts,
  models,
  temperatures = 0,
  replicates = 1L,
  schema = NULL,
  name = "default_design"
)

Arguments

prompts

Named (or unnamed) character vector of prompt templates. Templates may reference {text} and any additional column names in the input data frame passed to code_texts().

models

Character vector of model identifiers to cross with prompts.

temperatures

Numeric vector of sampling temperatures (>= 0). Default 0.

replicates

Positive integer number of stochastic replicates per (unit, prompt, model, temperature) cell. Default 1L.

schema

An coding_schema() object defining expected JSON fields. Defaults to a single numeric score field.

name

Optional descriptive name for the coding design.

Value

An object of class "llm_coding_design".

Examples

des <- coding_design(
  prompts = c(
    direct = "Rate emotional distress (1-7): {text}",
    rubric = "Using the clinical rubric, rate distress (1-7): {text}"
  ),
  models = c("model_a", "model_b"),
  temperatures = c(0, 0.5),
  schema = coding_schema(score = schema_field("numeric", min = 1, max = 7))
)
des
#> 
#> ── LLM Coding Design: default_design 
#> Prompts: 2 | Models: 2 | Temperatures: 2 | Replicates: 1
#> Cells per unit: 8
#> Models: "model_a" and "model_b"
#> Prompt IDs: "direct" and "rubric"
